items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I remember that one was named Ruby and he played Alto-sax. I never heard him play, but he and his buddy used to come to the hotel often in the afternoon after we had lunched and asked us questions about jazz music and musicians that they had heard about.

ctx.x: Edgar started making piano rolls but I never heard any that he made. Another thing that Saughtercamp told Hayes the night that he sat at our dining room table was that Edgar had forgotten more piano than he (Saughtercamp) would ever be able to play. That was a great compliment for Edgar Hayes coming from a man who was considered the best white dance band pianist in our part of the country.

Lee Rainey had a model T Ford coupe 4 to go to work in. It was supposed to hold only 3 people, but 4 of us used to crowd into it. Edgar Hayes was living at Lee Rainey's house with a girl who was supposed to be his wife that he had brought from Kentucky. Her name was Ruby and she was a real fine frame. We finished work around 2 every morning and it would take us about an hour to get to the Sterling Hotel from the Woodlawn Inn. Edgar Hayes, Lee Rainey, Edgar Courance and myself were the 4 that crowded into the…

Every morning as we were coming home Edgar Hayes had a song he would sing in the car. It was: 'I know where my baby is' and it never had any more words. He meant that he knew Ruby was home and waiting for him. Edgar Courance and I would get out of the car at the Sterling Hotel because we lived on Carlisle Avenue and it was not far for us to walk from the hotel. Lee and Edgar lived on West 9th Street between Cutter and Mound Street in front of the Y.M.C.A.
